When planting check the lower trunk and rootstocks of new trees for any bleeding symptoms and discard these
Do not allow the bud union to be buried
When growing and transplanting seedlings a copper fungicide can be applied to the seedbeds before sowing or holes before transplanting to prevent the disease (see yellow direct control)
Monitoring: Check for leaf yellowing and falling
Look for signs of gumming on the trunk and soil build up around the crown
Direct Control (Chemical): Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
Paint the trunks with copper oxychloride or hydroxide in early stages of infecton.
Remember to mix copper with vegetable oil so that it can stick.
Paint for 0.5-1m of the trunk from the ground

In the seedbed and when planting seedlings:
Copper oxychloride at the rate of 2.5kg in 15L water on seedbeds/holes before seedling emergence.
